name: multi-user-synthetic
description: Multi-user linear bandit: 5 instances of 50 users in 5 clusters, 500 actions in R^10, 20 random actions offered per step (as in CLUB and SCLUB), 2 runs each. LinUCB shared, per user, and per user with k-means clusters (5 clusters), against CLUB and SCLUB. Theoretical defaults.

policies.label: LinUCB
notes: lambda_=0.1 (any lambda > 0 keeps the bound valid)
delta=0.01 (any delta in (0, 1): the bound holds with probability 1 - delta)

policies.label: LinUCB_IND
notes: lambda_=0.1 (any lambda > 0 keeps the bound valid)
delta=0.01 (any delta in (0, 1): the bound holds with probability 1 - delta)

policies.label: LinUCB_IND_KMeans
notes: lambda_=0.1 (any lambda > 0 keeps the bound valid)
delta=0.01 (any delta in (0, 1): the bound holds with probability 1 - delta)

policies.label: CLUB
notes: alpha=1.0 (exploration weight, tuned on the data in the paper)
cluster_alpha=2.0 (tuned on the data in the paper)

policies.label: SCLUB
notes: cluster_alpha: 4 R sqrt(d / lambda_x), lambda_x from the actions offered

notices.title: Default hyperparameters
notices.text: All policies used the **values from their papers**: alpha=1 for LinUCB, LinUCB_IND and LinUCB_IND_KMeans; lambda_=1 for CLUB; alpha=1, lambda_=1 for SCLUB. LinUCB, LinUCB_IND and LinUCB_IND_KMeans used the **OFUL radius** (Abbasi-Yadkori et al., 2011). These values are safe in theory, except for LinUCB_IND_KMeans: it has **no regret guarantee** (see below). In practice, they often **explore too much**. The regret can then be higher than with tuned values.
notices.todo: Search the best values with param_grid=True. Or set them yourself, e.g. LinUCB(alpha=0.1).

notices.title: No regret guarantee
notices.text: LinUCB_IND_KMeans has **no proven regret bound**: k-means users are a heuristic. Its results can still be good, but nothing bounds its regret.
notices.default: Policies as in their papers: no projection, no buckets, no k-means (n_components=None, n_buckets=None, user_model="shared").
notices.todo: For a regret bound, pick a policy that has one (its docstring says), or turn off its heuristic option.

notices.title: Values with no theoretical choice
notices.text: Some policies kept defaults with **no value from theory**: lambda_=0.1 (any lambda > 0 keeps the bound valid) for all policies except CLUB and SCLUB; delta=0.01 (any delta in (0, 1): the bound holds with probability 1 - delta) for all policies except CLUB and SCLUB; alpha=1.0 (exploration weight, tuned on the data in the paper) for CLUB; cluster_alpha=2.0 (tuned on the data in the paper) for CLUB. Other values can give a lower or a higher regret.
notices.default: These values (each policy's docstring explains them).
notices.todo: Search them with param_grid, e.g. param_grid={"lambda_": [...]}. Or set them, e.g. LinUCB(lambda_=1).

notices.title: K-means users (heuristic)
notices.text: LinUCB_IND_KMeans pulled each user model towards the center of its k-means cluster. This is a heuristic: there is **no regret guarantee**.
notices.todo: Set user_model="individual" for one model per user.

notices.title: Not stored
notices.text: This run **did not store** the pseudo-regret and the action of every step. The charts cannot show them.
